messages:
maya: thinking out loud — we need a 'soft cutover' flow that routes traffic down two independent execution paths (canary variant + baseline) and picks the winner per-request with automatic fallback. wants low-latency decision and clear contract. any concerns?
rohan: +1. main tradeoffs: per-request arbitration adds p99 overhead if not careful, but gives fastest rollback. we should avoid sync decision in the hot path.
eva: agree. suggestion: do async scoring — attach a lightweight decision token to request, route to baseline by default, mirror to canary and update routing for subsequent requests from that user/session if canary looks healthy.
maya: curious about state: session affinity vs stateless token. session affinity helps UX for chat, but complicates routing service.
rohan: propose hybrid: cookie/session-level pinning for interactive sessions, but TTL short (e.g., 5-10 min) and explicit unpin on error. for stateless short requests, per-request fallback only.
sam: what about stale KV cache/kv-cache hits? if canary has different hidden-behavior we might serve stale responses. need invalidation strategy.
eva: invalidate on model-version-change or quantization toggles. also add response-signature hash to cache keys: model-v2|quant-q4|sig-<hash>.
maya: metrics + signals for auto-fallback? we need a concise set so routing can make decisions autonomously.
rohan: keep it minimal: error-rate, p99 latency delta vs baseline, hallucination/regression signals (from eval hooks), and a fast health-probe success ratio. each with short-window and long-window buffers.
eva: weight decisions: require at least two signals to breach thresholds before cutting traffic. prevents noisy single-metric flips.
ci-bot: build/test pipeline triggered: canary-rollout-sanity v3. logs: 8 tests passed, 2 flaky regressions flagged.
maya: nice. for interfaces: routing-service should expose a small API: /decide {model, customer, session, constraints} -> {path: baseline|canary, reason, token}. keep it sync but super lightweight (simple lookup + recent metrics).
sam: maybe return a 'shadow' flag: serve baseline but mirror to canary for telemetry until stable. reduces risk.
rohan: failure modes: routing-service outage. fallback plan: local deterministic fallback in client SDK (pin-to-baseline) + circuit that opens after N failures. document protocol version so clients can fallback safely.
eva: also, telemetry contract: emit route.decision events with token, model_version, reason, signals snapshot. needed for audits and offline analysis.
maya: quick config sketch (YAML):
```yaml
rollouts:
  - id: soft-cutover-v1
    baseline: model@2026-03-01
    candidate: model@2026-03-15
    autopilot:
      require: ["error_rate", "p99_latency"]
      thresholds:
        error_rate: 0.5%
        p99_latency: 1.25x
      windows: {short: 2m, long: 30m}
    affinity_ttl: 300s
    mirror_until: stable
```

rohan: good. operational runbook bits: 1) quick rollback endpoint, 2) emergency pin-all-to-baseline, 3) metrics-burn-in check before increasing traffic, 4) on-call alert for decision-service latency > 200ms.
sam: testing: unit test routing logic, e2e with canary mirror, synthetic traffic that simulates degraded tail latency.
eva: one more: privacy/tenancy: some customers need deterministic isolation — allow per-customer opt-out of mirroring/canary and force dedicated baseline lane.
maya: perfect. i'll turn this into a short RFC follow-up with interfaces, a proto sketch for /decide, and a proposed metrics set. want volunteers for review?
rohan: i'll take the proto + perf budget.
eva: i'll write the telemetry schema and runbook additions.
sam: i'll add cache invalidation and SDK fallback docs.
ci-bot: jira: PLAT-9923 created for soft-cutover design follow-up (assignee: maya).
